title: We gave 171 AI traders the real market, farmed them, and watched the results
author: _foursix_
selftext: Automated AI research and development and backtesting for AI farming over a hundred AI trading swarms, still adding more data repos, tools, and letting the AI farmer using Opus 5.5 at it. The farmer learns as he goes...

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 171 is a lot of swarms to keep honest. is the farmer scoring them on real orders or on simulated fills?

replies.author: _foursix_
replies.body:
we started with a single agent swarm, basically built an AI agent harness "queen bee" that wraps the LLM, so she has a full trading toolbox, market data, provenance, protective bias, guardrails, etc. etc. Then we multiplied it to test against different models and strategies.

Now we added a new AI "farmer" harness, who has access to historical market data (including options, earnings, etc), and is autonomously working the swarms on a daily basis—checking for errors, failed LLM calls, evaluating performance, retiring bad swarms, analyzing the "queen bee" trading discretion as she builds history (swarms are a hybrid of algorithmic and discretion/regime/news trading), backtesting and researching to develop and plant new swarms, making code fixes and pushing, keeping his own journal, straight from the Claude MCP connector in the cloud, all so we can sit back and watch. They start out on simulation, then the farmer graduates good ones to a brokerage paper account, then from there they can go live. Most swarms fail, but all you need is a few profitable ones, and that's the point. I use it with real money, and I like it. All trades, EOD reports, etc. are public and posted by the bots into our discord. We don't hide anything including the losers. Will be looking at integrating/adapting the Nous Hermes Agent as the farmer next.

We're now pretty much at the limit of what we can do because of compute power and costs, limited brokerage paper accounts, but the thing could be expanded into thousands of swarms and dozens of farmers working on them if AI usage + cloud compute + market data APIs + database + storage didn't all cost so much
